draft.exec:
Nusantara Mart loses orders when the site goes down during flash sales.

This proposal designs a storefront in Jakarta that absorbs 50x traffic spikes, queues every checkout request and keeps all data local.

The result is a store that stays up when sales open, protecting revenue and customer trust.

needs.need: Site goes down every flash sale and checkout gets slow.
needs.quote: site goes down every flash sale
needs.answer: Web servers scale out automatically while a queue buffers every checkout so the database never stalls. This keeps the storefront open and protects orders.

needs.need: Lost many orders during the last 11.11 event.
needs.quote: last 11.11 we lost a lot of orders
needs.answer: RocketMQ holds checkout requests until workers process them safely. No order is dropped even at peak load, directly recovering the revenue lost on 11.11.

needs.need: Traffic hits 50x normal within five minutes of a sale opening.
needs.answer: NLB handles massive TCP bursts from the app while Auto Scaling adds compute instantly. The storefront survives the spike without manual intervention.

needs.need: Almost all flash sale traffic comes from the mobile app.
needs.quote: almost all of it comes from our mobile app
needs.answer: HTTPDNS prevents DNS hijacking for app users and NLB routes raw TCP efficiently. Mobile shoppers reach the store faster and more reliably.

outcomes.title: Orders survive the spike
outcomes.text: RocketMQ buffers checkouts and dedicated workers drain them at a safe pace, so no order is dropped when traffic jumps 50x.

outcomes.title: Mobile app stays fast
outcomes.text: HTTPDNS resolves domains safely inside the app while NLB handles the raw TCP burst, keeping mobile shoppers connected during the first five minutes.

outcomes.title: Costs track demand
outcomes.text: Auto Scaling adds web and checkout servers only when needed and removes them after the sale, turning fixed capacity into variable cost.

outcomes.title: Data stays in Jakarta
outcomes.text: Every component runs in ap-southeast-5, keeping Nusantara Mart data within Indonesia as required.

why.dns: Routes public domain queries to the edge so shoppers find the store. Without it, customers cannot resolve the shop address.
why.httpdns: Prevents DNS hijacking for mobile shoppers who drive almost all flash sale traffic. Without it, app users face connection failures or redirection during sales.
why.esa: Caches product pages and absorbs attack traffic at the edge before it reaches Jakarta. Without it, origin servers face the full 50x spike directly.
why.alb: Distributes HTTP storefront traffic across two zones so one failure does not take the site down. Without it, a single zone outage stops sales.
why.waf: Blocks bot scalpers and injection attacks that target flash sales. Without it, bots buy inventory before real customers and attacks slow checkout.
why.nlb: Handles the massive TCP connection bursts from the mobile app during the first five minutes. Without it, standard load balancing drops connections under 50x load.
why.ecs: Runs the storefront and dedicated checkout workers in Jakarta. Without it, there is no compute to serve pages or process orders.
why.ess: Adds servers automatically when the 50x spike hits and removes them after. Without it, Nusantara Mart either pays for idle capacity or crashes during sales.
why.tair: Holds sessions and hot inventory counts in memory so the database survives flash sale reads. Without it, the database stalls under concurrent shopper load.
why.rds: Stores orders reliably across two zones in Jakarta. Without it, completed checkouts have no durable home and 11.11 losses repeat.
why.rocketmq: Buffers checkout requests so orders are never lost when traffic spikes 50x. Without it, the database overloads and orders drop like last 11.11.
why.oss: Stores product images that ESA caches at the edge. Without it, every image request hits origin servers and slows page loads during sales.
why.sls: Centralizes logs so the team can troubleshoot sale events quickly. Without it, diagnosing why checkout slowed takes hours instead of minutes.
why.cloudmonitor: Alerts on CPU, latency and queue depth before customers notice problems. Without it, the team reacts to outages instead of preventing them.

tradeoffs.text: Queue-based checkout adds slight delay before order confirmation appears in the app.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Show a processing status in the mobile app so shoppers know their order is secured.

tradeoffs.text: Auto Scaling needs time to provision instances during the sudden 50x spike.
tradeoffs.mitigation: Schedule scaling actions just before known flash sale start times.

tradeoffs.text: Running separate web and checkout worker fleets increases operational complexity.
tradeoffs.mitigation: CloudMonitor and SLS provide unified visibility across both fleets.

next: Confirm how your checkout backend is built today to size the worker fleet correctly.
Provide your peak order rate per minute during a flash sale to tune RocketMQ throughput.
Confirm whether the storefront must be public-facing or internal only.
Schedule a load test simulating the 50x spike to validate scaling rules before the next sale.
